Engine noise may indicate low oil level, worn components, or ignition problems. Please check oil level first.
Unusual engine sounds should be inspected quickly. It may be internal wear or poor combustion.
If the noise increases with acceleration, visit a mechanic immediately.
Engine overheating is often caused by low coolant or radiator issues. Stop driving and let the engine cool.
Check coolant level and radiator fan. Do not open radiator cap when hot.
Overheating can damage the engine. Seek mechanical inspection.
Your battery may be discharged. Try jump starting the vehicle.
Check battery terminals for corrosion and tight connections.
If the battery is old, replacement may be required.
A battery warning light often indicates alternator failure.
If the car loses power while driving, alternator output may be low.
Have the charging system tested at a service center.

Brake noise often indicates worn brake pads or debris in the braking system. If you hear grinding or experience reduced braking efficiency, it is recommended to inspect the brake pads and discs immediately for safety.
A soft brake pedal may suggest brake fluid leak or air in system.
Brake issues affect safety. Immediate inspection is recommended.
ABS warning means anti-lock braking system may not function correctly.
Normal braking may still work, but emergency braking control may be reduced.
Have the ABS system scanned for fault codes.
Engine oil should usually be changed every 5000 to 10000 km depending on vehicle type.
Regular oil changes improve engine life and performance.
Check your vehicle manual for recommended interval.
Low oil pressure is serious. Stop the engine immediately.
Check engine oil level before driving again.
Driving with low oil pressure can cause engine damage.
Check tire pressure using a pressure gauge.
Inflate tires to recommended PSI shown on door sticker.
Driving with low pressure reduces fuel efficiency and safety.
Replace the flat tire with spare tire if available.
Drive slowly to nearest service station.
Check for visible damage before driving.
Poor fuel economy may be due to dirty air filter or low tire pressure.
Aggressive driving and traffic also increase fuel usage.
Engine tuning and maintenance can improve efficiency.
